title: Cascade Health - Privacy, KMS & 'no-train' confirmation
summary: Review of data handling commitments (no training on customer data), encryption/KMS options, RBAC/SSO integration, audit logs and retention. Customer requested explicit verbiage for legal and a KMS key rotation walkthrough. Agreed next steps: send SOC2 package, KMS config examples, schedule short follow-up demo with infra team and legal.
action_items: Priya Shah | Send SOC 2 Type II attestation and security package | 2025-12-05
Daniel Ortiz | Share KMS key rotation whitepaper and sample terraform snippet | 2025-12-03
Omar Bello | Prepare short demo of VPC Private deployment + SAML SSO integration | 2025-12-10
Marta Ruiz | Share canonical list of PII/PHI fields to be flagged in prompts | 2025-12-08
next_steps: Redwood to email SOC2 + ISO docs and 'no training' legal wording
Schedule 30m technical demo for Cascade Infra + Legal (Doodle to follow)
Run short pilot: 1000 requests/day for 2 weeks to validate audit logs and KMS integration
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-11-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood CSM), Omar Bello (Redwood SE); Marta Ruiz (Cascade CISO), Ethan Patel (Head of ML), Sana Ali (Legal), Jon Weller (Infra)

[00:00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can folks say name and role?
[00:00:10] Marta Ruiz: Marta, CISO, Cascade. Hi.
[00:00:13] Ethan Patel: Ethan, Head of ML.
[00:00:15] Sana Ali: Sana, Legal.
[00:00:17] Jon Weller: Jon, Infra.
[00:00:19] Priya Shah: Great. From Redwood: Priya, Daniel, Lina and Omar. We're here to go over privacy commitments, KMS/encryption options and the specific language you wanted around no-training on customer data.
[00:00:35] Daniel Ortiz: I'll try to keep it technical and also show the KMS patterns we recommend across hosted vs private. 
[00:00:42] Marta Ruiz: Thanks. We mainly need an ironclad "we do not train on customer data" statement and to understand retention of prompts, logs and any transient storage. Also, KMS — we want to know if keys are customer-managed and rotation.
[00:00:58] Priya Shah: Understandable. High level: for Redwood Hosted we provide a "no-training" attestation — that we do not use customer prompt or response data to update models. For Private deployments, obviously you control the model and training. We'll share the signed legal verbiage soon.
[00:01:15] Sana Ali: When you say "attestation" — is that in the contract or a separate SOC addendum? Legal needs a short paragraph we can paste into our policy.
[00:01:23] Priya Shah: Good question. We typically include the clause in the MSA and can provide a one-page addendum that states: "Redwood will not use customer-provided prompts or generated outputs to train or improve models shared in the Hosted service" — we'll send the specific language. 
[00:01:39] Jon Weller: For audit, we need to see retention windows and the ability to purge. What's the default retention for logs, transcripts and KV/cache?
[00:01:47] Daniel Ortiz: Default telemetry and audit logs are 90 days in the console for hosted. You can configure log retention via the console up to 7 years for audit logs as part of enterprise plan. Prompt and response retention for Hosted API is configurable — default 30 days, can disable storage or configure shorter windows. There's also a KV/prefix cache which is in-memory and ephemeral unless you use caching with explicit persistence — that persists in your configured store if you attach one.
[00:02:12] Marta Ruiz: So if we set "no retention" on prompts, are there any transient copies that could end up in S3 or elsewhere?
[00:02:19] Daniel Ortiz: For Hosted with retention disabled, we still have ephemeral in-flight buffers — things that exist in process or RAM — but we don't persist them to disk or S3. The only exceptions are if you enable debugging/logging for a customer session — that's opt-in and gated behind support/consent.
[00:02:36] Sana Ali: We need that explicitly in writing — especially the part about not persisting to disk or S3. Also need the mechanism to prove it in audits.
[00:02:45] Priya Shah: Absolutely. We'll include the technical description and the SOC 2 mapping that shows controls around log handling — that'll help for audit readiness.
[00:02:53] [00:03:00] Ethan Patel: Quick question on the phrase "no training" — does that cover fine-tuning or only the base model training? If I send a dataset to any Redwood endpoint, could that be used for fine-tuning later?
[00:03:12] Daniel Ortiz: Good nuance. Our Hosted policy: we do not use customer prompts/outputs to train, fine-tune, or update the shared models. If a customer explicitly opts into a fine-tuning service — which is a separate workflow and explicit opt-in with data ownership preserved — then that data is used only for that customer's private fine-tune artifact, not for general model improvements.
[00:03:31] Marta Ruiz: How is that opt-in gated? Is there an API flag or a separate service?
[00:03:36] Omar Bello: It's a separate service currently; we require an agreement and specific API calls. There's also RBAC so only certain users can trigger fine-tune jobs.
[00:03:44] Jon Weller: About KMS: do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) in hosted? We want to maintain control over the encryption keys and key rollover.
[00:03:52] Daniel Ortiz: Yes — we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS in Hosted mode (bring-your-own-key). You can supply an AWS KMS key ARN; we encrypt at rest using envelope encryption. We also support GCP KMS and Azure Key Vault in equivalent fashions for respective regions.
[00:04:08] Jon Weller: Can we rotate keys on our side and revoke access? What's the failover behaviour if key is revoked?
[00:04:16] Daniel Ortiz: If you rotate keys properly (create new key and update the ARN), the service supports key rotation with no downtime. If a key is revoked without updating, accesses to encrypted artifacts that use that key will fail — we'll have a documented key-rotation procedure and we can run a DR tabletop with your team.
[00:04:33] Marta Ruiz: We also need to know about audit logs for key usage — who accessed which key and when.
[00:04:38] Daniel Ortiz: KMS usage logs are captured in the cloud provider's audit logs (CloudTrail, Stackdriver, Azure Monitor). Redwood can surface those entries in our console and export them to your S3/GCS/Blob store if you want long-term storage.
[00:04:51] [00:05:00] Sana Ali: On the RBAC/SSO front — we have strict role separation. How granular can Redwood's RBAC get? We need read-only auditors, service accounts for ML ops, and admins.
[00:05:10] Priya Shah: Our RBAC supports built-in roles and custom roles. You can create roles scoped to workspaces, models, and routes. SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning is supported for enterprise plans.
[00:05:22] Lina Park: Also there's token-level scoping for API keys — you can restrict tokens to specific models and quota.
[00:05:27] Ethan Patel: Does RBAC tie into KMS? Meaning can I restrict who can attach a CMK to a deployment?
[00:05:33] Daniel Ortiz: Yes. You can restrict who can update deployment-level settings including the key ARN. That's enforced via RBAC and audited.
[00:05:40] Marta Ruiz: Good. About logs: we need a signed statement about immutable audit logs and exportability.
[00:05:46] Priya Shah: We'll provide the SOC mapping and a short note on immutability — for Hosted, audit logs are write-once in our system and you can forward copies to customer-owned storage. For Dedicated or Private, you control the storage entirely.
[00:06:00] [00:06:15] Jon Weller: In a security incident, how quickly can we get a list of requests tied to a user or API key?
[00:06:21] Omar Bello: We can surface request-level logs within minutes; for deeper forensics we pull raw logs and can deliver within an agreed SLA depending on plan. We also have tracing IDs which you can pass from your app into Redwood and we persist that correlation id.
[00:06:35] Ethan Patel: About PII/PHI detection — do you provide built-in classifiers to flag PII or PHI in prompts?
[00:06:42] Daniel Ortiz: Yes we have content filters and an optional PII detection package that can redact or flag fields. It's configurable — you can choose to mask in transit, mask before storage, or block requests entirely. We'll share the docs and sample policy.
[00:06:55] Marta Ruiz: Does the PII detector run locally for private deployments?
[00:06:58] Daniel Ortiz: For Private deployments, yes, the detection runs inside your VPC/on-prem and never leaves your network unless configured to.
[00:07:05] Sana Ali: For legal: can you confirm the phrase: "Redwood does not use customer prompts or outputs to train or improve models in the Hosted service unless explicitly contracted"?
[00:07:15] Priya Shah: Yes, we can confirm that wording; we'll provide exact legal-approved phrasing.
[00:07:21] [00:07:30] Ethan Patel: A small thing — you mentioned prefix/KV cache earlier. If we use the prefix cache, are cached items encrypted with the CMK?
[00:07:38] Daniel Ortiz: Cached items persisted to storage use the same envelope encryption as other artifacts — yes, encrypted with the CMK if you attach one. In-memory cache is ephemeral and not persisted.
[00:07:48] Jon Weller: For compliance, we need proof of key lifecycle — Rotations, who rotated, and when. Does Redwood log key admin actions?
[00:07:57] Omar Bello: Yes, key admin actions are in the audit trail and we can export CloudTrail events. We'll put an example export with sample entries.
[00:08:06] Marta Ruiz: Can we get signed attestations for SOC 2 controls relevant to key management and data handling?
[00:08:11] Priya Shah: Yes, SOC 2 Type II covers those controls. We'll send the attestation and a control mapping.
[00:08:18] [00:08:30] Sana Ali: If we require data residency — specific EU region — can Redwood pin a tenant to eu-west-1 only?
[00:08:38] Daniel Ortiz: We can pin deployments to regions. Hosted can be regionally isolated; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private for full guarantee.
[00:08:47] Ethan Patel: Another question on logs: is there a signed cryptographic hash option to prove immutability?
[00:08:53] Daniel Ortiz: We don't currently offer signed ledger hashes out-of-the-box, but customers can forward logs to an append-only store you control and we can include checksums. We can discuss custom solutions.
[00:09:06] [00:09:20] Priya Shah: (to Legal) Sana, are there specific wording edits you want to see?
[00:09:24] Sana Ali: I'd like three things: 1) Exact "no training" clause; 2) Clarify ephemeral/transient buffers not persisted; 3) A purge API with SLA.
[00:09:34] Priya Shah: All doable. We have a purge API for Hosted — immediate deletion request, and we return a job id and estimated completion; for audit we can provide proof of deletion. We'll include SLA details.
[00:09:46] Marta Ruiz: What about backups? Could deleted prompts remain in backups?
[00:09:50] Daniel Ortiz: Backups are encrypted and subject to retention policies; when you request deletion, we scrub active storage and rotate any backups that might contain data, and we have a documented process for that. We'll include the RTO/RPO numbers in the doc.
[00:10:06] [00:10:20] Jon Weller: For the pilot, we want to validate that an external auditor could see all necessary traces. Is that something Redwood can support — providing a read-only auditor role?
[00:10:28] Lina Park: Yes — we can create read-only auditor accounts scoped to the data needed, and we support SAML federation for auditors too.
[00:10:34] Ethan Patel: Great. For the demo, can you show the audit trail for a single request — from API key to KMS usage to log entry?
[00:10:41] Omar Bello: Yes, in the follow-up demo we can replay an example request and show the correlation id across CloudTrail, console audit, and the request log.
[00:10:49] [00:11:00] Priya Shah: Ok — quick recap before we move to Q&A: 1) Redwood will send SOC2/ISO docs and the MSA clause for "no training"; 2) Daniel/Omar will prepare KMS rotation docs and sample config; 3) we'll schedule a 30m demo with your infra and legal (Jon, Sana and Ethan). Anything else?
[00:11:18] Marta Ruiz: I'd like a small table in the docs that maps controls to our internal policy — e.g., "Key rotation" -> CloudTrail evidence -> export instructions.
[00:11:25] Priya Shah: Noted. We'll include a controls mapping table.
[00:11:29] Sana Ali: Also want explicit examples of language we can send to auditors — e.g., "Redwood does not train on our data" with signer name and date.
[00:11:37] Priya Shah: We'll provide a signed template.
[00:11:40] [00:11:50] Ethan Patel: One last technical nit: concurrency and KV cache — if we enable persistent prefix cache backed by a customer bucket, what's the expected latencies?
[00:11:58] Daniel Ortiz: If it's in the same region and using GCS/S3 optimized access, added latency is small — sub-10ms for cache hits; we'll provide benchmark numbers for your expected QPS.
[00:12:09] Jon Weller: Any risk of leaked PII into logs when using debugging?
[00:12:13] Daniel Ortiz: Debugging will capture full request/response — we only enable with explicit consent. It is treated as sensitive and subject to the same encryption and retention policies you choose.
[00:12:22] [00:12:30] Lina Park: I'll drop links after the call: SOC2 package, KMS how-to, purge API docs, and RBAC/SSO setup guide.
[00:12:37] Priya Shah: Perfect. We'll aim to get those to you by end of week.
[00:12:41] Marta Ruiz: Timeline — we want to be production-ready in Q1; likely pilot in mid-December.
[00:12:46] Priya Shah: Sounds good. We'll align calendars.
[00:12:50] [00:13:00] Sana Ali: Thanks everyone.
[00:13:02] Priya Shah: Thanks — we'll follow up with the package and the meeting invite for the demo.

(Transcription notes: occasional overlap, some proper nouns mis-heard by the transcription engine e.g., "prefix cache" sometimes transcribed as "prefixed cash" in auto-captions — cleaned minimally for readability.)
